comments.text: Lived in Hungary from 2016-2019, Somogymegye county. Unfortunately, had to move to Ireland due to work. I still remember how some friends give negative response when i told them that we going to move to Hungary. Ends up that I LOVE that country, the neighbors they're soooooo kind, even though I had limited Magyar. An atmosphere that I don't find somewhere else, really. Still remember, in the summer time, I found somebody hanging a bags of fruit (cherry, peach, apple etc) or sometimes a bottle of homemade wine, in our gate. How I miss Hungary so much. I am Indonesian, but I wish to have a house for retired in a rural Hungary, one day.

comments.author: @fowlarch
comments.text: Have been to Budapest a few times, simply love it! A very.close friend has his villa on Lake Balaton on one of the volcanic hills. He has a little winery in it too. There's also a lovely heritage village that a lady architect during Communist times saved, a lovely time capsule of traditional Hungarian rural architecture. It has an ancient site inside , mostly rocks, that must be thousands on years old. We drove all round the lake. It took a day. Budapest has a fantastic variety of architectural styles from Art Noveau, Art Deco, etc. Great people! Planning my next visit later this year.

comments.author: @bayingblade5532
comments.text: My seventh visit to this beautiful country coming up in August. I have experienced Budapest numerous times, Visigrad, Esztergom, Szentendre and the Balaton.  There are no huge mountains, no great outcrops, no bottomless lakes........just beauty around every corner.....culture, history and an atmosphere like nowhere else. I have discovered fabulous food and wine and grow to love this place a little more every time I visit. This year, I will be spending a few days in Tokaj, in a hotel in the middle of a vineyard with its own winery. I have a feeling that my love of Hungary will only grow further!
